name: aws-sagemaker-demand-forecasting-example
what_it_holds: MIT-licensed worked example (also mirrored as an official aws-samples repo) forecasting demand with AWS SageMaker XGBoost using PredictHQ event features as exogenous regressors.
why_useful: Another event-driven demand-forecasting method template (events -> XGBoost demand forecast) that could be adapted to nights/ADR around World Cup or major conferences, though it depends on a live PredictHQ feed rather than committed data.

why_all: Another event-driven demand-forecasting method template (events -> XGBoost demand forecast) that could be adapted to nights/ADR around World Cup or major conferences, though it depends on a live PredictHQ feed rather than committed data.
A concrete, runnable nowcasting-with-mixed-frequency-events template (gap #17) that could be adapted to regress ABNB nights/ADR residuals on an event-density feature built from PredictHQ.

name: jfjelstul/worldcup (Fjelstul World Cup Database)
what_it_holds: 27 linked datasets (>1.5M data points) on tournaments, teams, players, managers, referees, stadiums, matches, goals, bookings for all 22 men's World Cups (1930-2022) and 9 women's World Cups (1991-2019); available as R package, .RData, .csv, .json, and SQLite.
why_useful: Deep historical World Cup base-rate data (host-city attendance/stadium capacity patterns) useful for calibrating how prior World Cups moved host-country travel/lodging demand, though it stops at 2022 and does not itself cover 2026.
themes: Event calendars: FIFA World Cup 2026 schedule and host-city data, Olympics, concerts (Setlist.fm, Songkick, Ticketmaster API), conferences, PredictHQ samples, holiday calendars by country
why_all: Deep historical World Cup base-rate data (host-city attendance/stadium capacity patterns) useful for calibrating how prior World Cups moved host-country travel/lodging demand, though it stops at 2022 and does not itself cover 2026.

name: nager/Nager.Date
what_it_holds: Open-source public-holiday data and a free REST API (nagerholidays.com/api/v3) covering 200+ countries; holiday objects carry date, local/English name, country code, subdivision, and type (Public/Bank/School/Authorities/Optional/Observance); MIT licensed, 1.4k stars, 1,706 commits, also ships as NuGet/Docker.
why_useful: Alternative/cross-check source to the Python `holidays` package for per-country holiday calendars, reachable via a plain HTTP GET with no auth for a quick one-off pull (e.g. from a notebook without pandas/holidays installed).

name: peopledoc/workalendar
what_it_holds: Python module computing legal/religious holidays and working-day arithmetic for 80+ countries/territories including US state-level, Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, Chile, China, Japan, Korea, India, Australia, NZ, South Africa and more; includes precomputed astronomical data (equinoxes, solar terms) for 1991-2051; MIT license, ~1,377 commits, 950 stars.
why_useful: Second independent holiday/working-day calendar engine with stronger LatAm/APAC subdivision coverage than some alternatives, useful for regional (LatAm/APAC) seasonality controls referenced in gap #11 and cross-checking the `holidays` package.
time_coverage: 1991-2051 for astronomical holidays; general holiday rules for any year
themes: Event calendars: FIFA World Cup 2026 schedule and host-city data, Olympics, concerts (Setlist.fm, Songkick, Ticketmaster API), conferences, PredictHQ samples, holiday calendars by country
why_all: Second independent holiday/working-day calendar engine with stronger LatAm/APAC subdivision coverage than some alternatives, useful for regional (LatAm/APAC) seasonality controls referenced in gap #11 and cross-checking the `holidays` package.

name: tech-conferences/conference-data (confs.tech backing data)
what_it_holds: JSON files (one per topic/year) of tech conferences worldwide with fields for name, start/end dates, city/country location, CFP dates, social handles; 13,987 commits, community-maintained, MIT license, covers many years across dozens of tech topics (JS, Python, Rust, data, etc.).
why_useful: A machine-readable conference calendar with dates and host cities that can proxy business-travel demand spikes in specific ABNB markets (partial coverage of the 'conferences' part of gap #11); skewed toward software/tech conferences only, not a general conference census.
last_activity: actively maintained (19 open PRs, 4 open issues at capture)
